animations.title: A tile's picture becomes the player's
animations.trigger: tap a tile; its audio arrives
animations.now: Loader appears in one frame. When audio lands, a copy of the tile's picture flies 380ms over the loader (both z-index 60) to the player; the loader vanishes in one frame at 450ms or later.
animations.verdict: Broken hand-off: two pictures of one episode on screen, and the one people watched develop never moves. One element must travel the whole way (Replacements).
animations.notes:
What happens today. pointerdown records the tapped picture (Motion's `tapped`, index.html:5955-5966: the tile's .seed-img, its box and radius) and keeps it 8s. generate() shows #famLoading in one frame (8397) and paintLoadingVariant('daily') draws the tile's thumb in .fam-dev-pic (7569). When audio starts, onGenerationStarted (7660) calls finishGenOverlay - which clears at once if the loader has been up 450ms (GEN_MIN_VISIBLE_MS, 7313), else on a timer - and then navigate('player'). Motion.screen('player-open') (6030) makes a .motion-ghost of the TILE's picture at the tile's box and flies it 380ms to #playerBg. The ghost is appended to .frame after #famLoading, both z-index 60, so it paints over the loader.
Ready tile (the common case: editions are written and voiced ahead, §359/§610): audio at ~150-400ms, the ghost flies out of the rail position across the loader while the loader's own picture sits in the middle half-developed; at 450ms the loader cuts out mid-flight. Unwritten tile: the loader cuts out in the same frame the player opens, the rails flash back under a 240ms fade, and the small tile picture grows. Over 8s, it is a push slide instead (bug list).
Fix (B): in Motion.screen, when #famLoading is .active.alt and holds a seen .fam-dev-pic, use that element as the source (its box, its picture, 16px radius), hide it, fly it 340ms to #playerBg, fade the loader's kicker/title/status 150ms ease-in and its background 200ms, and remove .active when the flight lands. finishGenOverlay's 450ms floor still decides WHEN the hand-off starts, so it never shows less than today. Audio is already playing; the player screen is active from its first frame underneath - nothing is held. A tile with no picture (drawing only) keeps the push, with the loader fading 150ms.
Interrupt: a second tap or the X calls clearGenOverlay; settle() finishes any flight at once (Motion.screen already does this). The player-open flight itself is the lead's shared item; this changes only its source when the DailyFAM loader is up, so coordinate with the lead's deck.
Reduced motion: loader goes at once; the player's 120ms crossfade stays (today's rule).

animations.title: Picture Develop (DailyFAM's wait)
animations.trigger: tap a tile no friends have heard
animations.now: Picture goes blur(16px) grey to sharp over 2.4s (.2,.7,.2,1) while scaling .94 to 1; a sheen sweeps every 1.6s on bare ease-in-out. Ready tiles leave at 450ms, still mid-blur.
animations.verdict: The owner's pick (§592), kept. On the common ready tile it ends half-developed (Peak-end); the scale is a 2.4s move; the sheen's curve is a keyword; reduced motion freezes every indicator.
animations.notes:
Code: .fam-dev.develop .fam-dev-pic runs famDevelop 2.4s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1) both: from blur(16px) grayscale(1) brightness(1.4) scale(.94) to none (2294-2299). Its ::after sheen is a white band, translateX(-120%) to 120%, 1.6s, 0.4s delay, ease-in-out, infinite (2295-2300). Title rises with famLdUp .3s ease (2277). The status dot pulses (famLdPulse 1.2s, 2281).
The loader is shown at least 450ms (GEN_MIN_VISIBLE_MS) and goes when audio arrives. Most DailyFAM taps are ready (written and voiced ahead), so audio lands in a few hundred ms and the screen goes at 450ms: on (.2,.7,.2,1) at 0.19 of 2.4s the picture is about 6px blurred, 40% grey and washed out. The last frame people see of the owner's pick is a soft, greyish picture - the end they remember (Peak-end).
Option B keys the speed on the tile's own `cached` flag (myFamTopics[t.loaderTopic].cached, already on every tile and used for the READY badge): ready = 420ms ease-out, so it is sharp a beat before the 450ms floor and the hand-off (tile-to-player B) carries a finished picture; unwritten = today's 2.4s, then the sheen keeps saying 'working'. A 'ready' tile whose audio is slow just sits sharp with the sheen running - still honest. Option C reads the four marks pollGenSteps already fetches for the daily loader (7455: contextualized, retrieved, verified, written) and steps the blur down per mark; it shows no list and holds nothing, but it is §148's progress in another form, which §509 reserved for search and Go Deeper - an owner call.
Drop the scale in every option: it is a 2.4s movement, over the 450ms limit, and blur alone reads as focus. Blur stays at 16px (under the skill's 20px). Sheen on linear: it represents time passing, like a spinner.
Reduced motion today turns off develop, sheen, title rise AND the status dot (2346-2356), so nothing on the screen says it is alive. The skill keeps indicators moving: keep the dot's pulse in all options, picture sharp, sheen off.

animations.title: Friends Gather (DailyFAM's wait)
animations.trigger: tap a tile friends have heard
animations.now: Up to 3 faces fly in from up to 230px away in straight lines, scale .4 to 1, 600ms with overshoot (.2,1.3,.4,1), 160ms apart; the names line rises at 700ms. Ready tiles leave at 450ms.
animations.verdict: The owner's pick (§592), but on a ready tile (gone at 450ms) the third face has not started and the line naming them never shows. Also over 450ms, overshooting, straight-line travel.
animations.notes:
Code: .fam-dev-faces .src-mark (44px, 3px page-colour border) famFaceIn .6s cubic-bezier(.2,1.3,.4,1) both, from translate(--fx,--fy) scale(.4) opacity 0; offsets (-130,-170), (40,-230), (190,-130) with delays .12/.28/.44s (2302-2309). The names line (friendsListenedLine: 'Maya, Jordan and 4 others listened') is famLdUp .3s .7s both (2310). The picture is sharp; no sheen, so the only 'working' sign is the status dot.
Ready case: the loader leaves at 450ms (GEN_MIN_VISIBLE_MS). On the overshoot curve face 1 is just past its spot and face 2 about 90% there, but face 3 starts at 440ms and the names line at 700ms: the line that says WHO listened - the screen's point - never shows. Unwritten case: it plays fully, but 600ms with a 30% overshoot is past the project's 450ms ceiling and the skill's no-bounce rule, the 160ms stagger is 3-4x the skill's 30-50ms for copies, and two-axis travel over 40px should arc.
A (recommended): faces appear where they will sit, rising 12px from scale .9, 260ms ease-out, 40ms apart (done at 340ms); names line fades in with the first face (+60ms). Readable before any hand-off. B: each face starts where it sat on the tapped card's dark faces pill (.seed-friends .friend-face, 22px, bottom right of the tile's picture; the boxes can be read on pointerdown like Motion's `tapped`), and arcs (peak 15% of distance, the skill's arc() technique: x on one curve, y lifted by sin) to the loader's corner, 22px growing to 44px (scale .5 to 1), 360ms ease-in-out, 40ms apart: last lands at 440ms - right at the edge of a ready tile's 450ms. C keeps today's flight for unwritten tiles only, and draws a ready tile's faces already landed.
With tile-to-player B, the faces stay on the picture as it flies (children of .fam-dev). Avatars: the cached-image flash (bug list) applies here too - draw img opacity 1 when complete.
Reduced motion: faces and names drawn in place at once; the status dot keeps pulsing.

animations.title: Pick up and faces rows land late
animations.now: Rails draw first; /api/godeeper then inserts 'Pick up where you left off' (up to ~260px) above them in one frame, and /api/circle can insert the faces row (~100px): the rails jump down.
animations.verdict: A layout jump on the page's main open, often during the rails' arrive. Reads should show what was there last time, then reconcile (Doherty); only a real change should move.
animations.notes:
Order today (loadMyFamFeed, 16318): skeleton in #myfamFeed (first open only); loadMyFamCircle() fires /api/circle; /api/myfam lands and renderMyFamFeed draws the rails (Motion.arriveRails); only then loadGoDeeper() fires /api/godeeper (16344), whose renderGoDeeper (16230) fills #goDeeperBlock - ABOVE #myfamFeed - with the heading and up to 4 cards (2 rows of 80-104px). The rails drop by the block's height in one frame. /api/circle usually answers first, but when it does not, paintMyFamCircle (17646) un-hides a ~100px row above everything. On later opens (every tab tap, openMyFamTab 14937) both blocks are re-rendered from scratch: same height, no jump, unless something changed - which is exactly when the listener has just stopped an episode half-way and a new Pick up card appears.
A thumb aiming at a rail tile can land on a different tile when the rails drop 260px under it (Fitts). The project rule 'nothing on the page-load path awaits' rules out holding the rails for the block.
B (recommended): keep the last Pick up answer and circle per account on the device (famLastFeed already does this for the rails, 10497; same per-device rule, emptied on log-out) and paint them on the first frame with the rails; when the answers land, diff by query/user id: an added card fades up 8px (260ms ease-out), a gone one recedes (fade + scale .95, 150ms ease-in) and the rest FLIP to their new cells (200ms ease-in-out). Identical answers change nothing. animations.notes:
Code: .story-bar i {width:0}; .story-bar.on i {animation: storyFill var(--story-ms, 6000ms) linear forwards}; storyFill from width 0 to 100% (3203-3208); paused with animation-play-state (3207). showStory rebuilds the bars and restarts the fill on a fresh node (17792-17799). pauseStory/resumeStory (17813-17825) keep the 6s timer in step; a hold is STORY_HOLD_MS 220 (17892) and adds .held, whose rule carries `transition: opacity .2s` (3235) - so hiding fades 200ms on the default ease, and removing .held drops the transition with it, so the chrome returns in one frame.
Width forces layout on every frame for 6s, on a screen that also runs the cube turn and grow; scaleX on the <i> with transform-origin left is compositor-only and pauses the same way. .story-bar has overflow hidden and a 2px radius: scaleX squashes the <i>'s own corners, invisible at 2.5px tall.
Holding is a many-times gesture in a story; the skill's frequency rule allows no transition, and its exit rule wants exits shorter than entrances. A: hide 150ms ease-in, return 200ms ease-out. B: keep the bars visible while held (they are what says 'paused') and thicken the active one; head and reply row hide. C: both instant.
Under reduced motion the fill keeps running in all options (a progress indicator - the skill's one exception) and the chrome cuts at once.

animations.verdict: The owner's pick (§298), kept. Grow from the ring's own centre, and let the ring turn grey after the story has closed into it (Staging: chain, never overlap).
animations.notes:
Code: openCircleProfile (18230) opens the story when the person has vibes up; openStoryAt (17743) un-hides #storyOverlay, draws it and calls Motion.growStory, which reads pressedCircle (6433): the last pressed element's closest button - on the faces row that is the whole .yf-friend button, ring 72px plus a 6px gap plus the name, so the circle's centre is about 10px below the face's. It clips circle(r at centre) to circle(diagonal) over 300ms, EASE. closeStory (17954) calls shrinkStory first: an inert copy shrinks back to that circle in 240ms EASE_IO, fading out over its last 15%; the real overlay is hidden on the same frame, and then the rings are recomputed - fresh (gold gradient) to seen (grey, thinner) - in one frame, under the shrinking copy.
A (recommended): measure the .yf-ring inside the pressed button (or the .yf-friend's first child) for the centre and radius; grow on the skill's ease-out, shrink on its in-out (a shared-element move back, not an exit); then chain the ring: draw the seen ring as a second layer under the gold one and fade the gold out 200ms when the shrink lands (+240ms). The ring's padding and border width change between states (3169-3173), so put both looks on stacked layers rather than transitioning padding.
B adds Instagram's drag-down to close (Jakob's law): pointermove after a vertical start (dy > dx) moves the overlay 1:1 and scales it by mapRange(dy, 0-300px, 1-.85); release past 80px or faster than 0.1px/ms closes with shrinkStory from the dragged position; else it springs back (400ms, bounce 0 - a CSS linear() spring, inside the 450ms limit). It must not fight the hold (220ms, cancelled by movement) or the sideways swipe (|dx| > |dy| x 1.2).
Reduced motion: story shows and hides at once, ring changes at once (today too).

animations.title: Turning to the next friend's story
animations.trigger: swipe sideways, or a friend's vibes run out
animations.now: A swipe is read only on release (50px or more); then a 340ms cube turn (perspective 900px, (.4,0,.2,1)) plays. Both faces stay fully lit; the story never moves under the finger.
animations.verdict: The owner's pick (§298). The skill wants a drag to be direct (Interruptible) and a turn to be lit (Solid drawing): follow the finger, darken the face turning away.
animations.notes:
Code: the overlay's pointerdown/up (17899-17929) records the start and, on pointerup, treats |dx| >= 50 and |dx| > |dy| x 1.2 as a swipe: storyFriend(dir) then turnToFriend, which calls Motion.turnStory (6464): a black .motion-story-back, an inert copy of the old story rotating away (origin at its outer edge, rotateY to -90, translateX -100%) and the real overlay rotating in from 90, both 340ms EASE_IO, backface hidden, perspective(900px). Running out of vibes (storyStep) uses the same turn on its own clock.
Interruptible: 'drags are direct: the element stays 1:1 under the finger with no easing, and a spring takes over on release, carrying the release velocity.' Today the finger moves 50-150px with nothing following it, then the turn plays as a canned 340ms. B (recommended): on the first sideways pointermove past 12px (which already cancels the hold), draw the next friend's story into the real overlay and keep the copy (as turnStory does), then map dx to progress p = clamp(|dx| / width) and set both transforms per frame (straight-ahead: driven by input). Release: p > 1/3 or velocity > 0.1px/ms completes; else it turns back and restores the copy as the story. Use a spring-shaped CSS linear() curve over 400ms (inside the 450ms limit) or WAAPI with currentTime. At the first or last friend, rubber-band: dead zone 12px, resistance 150, ceiling 64px.
Solid drawing (A and B): a black overlay on each face, opacity 0 to .3 on the face turning away and .3 to 0 on the face arriving, mapped to the same progress.
The story timer: pause on drag start (pauseStory), resume on cancel; a completed turn shows the next story and its bars start.
Reduced motion: the next friend's story appears at once (today too); a drag moves nothing until release.

animations.title: A reply sent from a story
animations.trigger: type in the reply box and send
animations.now: The box clears and loses focus in one frame; 'Sent to Maya' shows on the bottom line. The heart turns red in one frame (the app's likes burst elsewhere).
animations.verdict: A sent message rises (Make it mean something): show the words leaving toward the friend instead of vanishing. The heart's burst belongs to the shared like (lead's deck).
animations.notes:
Code: sendStoryReply (18053) reads the input, empties it, blurs it (which resumes the story via storyReplyBlur after 60ms) and posts /api/messages; success is toast('Sent to ' + name), failure the server's sentence. likeStory (18064) flips aria-pressed (CSS turns the icon #FF4D5E and filled, 3406) and sends a heart message once per story.
The words vanish: the person sees an empty box and, a moment later, a line at the bottom of the screen. 'An item leaves toward where it went: a sent message rises.' A: before clearing, copy the input's text into an inert span at the input's box (Motion's inertCopy pattern), clear the real input on the same frame, and move the copy up 24px while it fades, 220ms ease-in (an exit); the bottom line confirms as today. B: the destination is the friend - their avatar sits at the top left of the story (#storyAv): a small copper bubble with the first words arcs there (the skill's arc: x on ease-out, y lifted by a sine, peak 15%), scaling to .4, 360ms; the avatar bumps 1.15 (220ms) on arrival - two chained motions (Staging). It crosses the story's own content, and the story resumes underneath it. C: as today.
A failed send: the bottom line names the failure; the words are not put back today (keep everything the person entered - Errors: recover): restore the text into the box on failure in every option.
Heart: list-only - it should use the same burst-and-label the rest of the app's likes use (shared item), so it is not an option here.
Reduced motion: box clears at once; bottom line confirms.

animations.title: Taking a tile away
animations.trigger: Not interested in a tile's ⋯; the X on a Pick up card
animations.now: Not interested: tile and gap vanish in the frame the sheet starts fading; no Undo. Pick up X (20px): card gone, grid reflows in one frame, then redrawn again by the server's answer.
animations.verdict: Both are permanent and both lose where the thing went. One removal for the page (Similarity): a copy leaves, the rest close the gap, Undo for 5s (Errors: recover).
animations.notes:
Code: openTileMenu (10303) is the shared sheet; showActionSheet runs closeSheet() then the action (11258), so the sheet fades 150ms while tileNotInterested (10325) records not_interested at once, drops the tile from railTiles and removes every [data-topic=id] (rails and View more), then shows 'Got it - you'll see less like this' with no action. dismissGoDeeper (16273) redraws the block without the card, POSTs /api/godeeper/dismiss, and on OK calls loadGoDeeper, which redraws again (a second one-frame change if the server's list differs). Both are permanent: not_interested is read over the whole history (§499); a dismissed card 'never offered again' on every device. The X is 20x20 (1877), under the 24px floor, in the corner of a card whose own tap plays it.
One motion for both (Similarity), with the owner's §298 removed-row timings (out 180ms, gap 200ms) so a removal looks the same in Queue, Saved, the rails and Pick up. A (recommended): the data changes at once (the owner's 'leaves at once'); an inert copy put back where the tile was fades and nudges 12px down - exits move a little, never their full size - then the neighbours FLIP into the gap (measure before, remove, translate from the old x/y to 0). Not interested waits for the sheet's 150ms exit before the copy moves (Staging). If Pick up empties, the block closes with the grid-rows expander (190ms) so the rails rise instead of jumping.
Undo: the bottom line's action ('Undo'; the snack supports one, but holds actions 3.5s today, §299 - the skill wants 5s) for 5s; the event or dismiss is sent when the line closes or the page hides, so Undo only redraws. Undo reverses: the gap opens (200ms) and the tile fades up 8px (260ms). The X gets a 44x44 zone (::after; the corner has no neighbour).
B: the copy tips back (rotateX to 20deg, perspective 700px) and shrinks to .9 as it fades; the last neighbour settles 30ms after the rest (follow through). C: today's instant removal, plus Undo and the 44px zone.
Reduced motion: removal and gap at once; Undo the same.

options.tradeoff: Needs the request deferred until the Undo line closes, so a page closed in those 5s must still send it (on pagehide).
options.why: The owner's own removed-row timings (§298), so removal reads the same across the app, and Undo makes two permanent actions safe.

Bottom line 'Got it - you'll see less like this · Undo'. 2500ms tap Undo: the gap opens (200ms) and tile 2 fades up back in (260ms). Loop.
